plain.li: Somebody mentioned rain at supper and I was off, telling about the week it rained on us out on the road. I can't seem to help it.
The young ones keep asking about the journey. I've told the river crossing so often it's starting to improve.

warm.li: I tell the road stories to anyone who sits still long enough, and they mostly let me finish.

blunt.li: Yes, I'm telling the one about the pass again. Sit down.

cheerful.li: I've got a story of the road for every occasion now! Weddings, funerals, bad weather, good stew.

gloomy.li: I keep telling the road stories. Some of the people in them didn't make it here.

cold.li: I tell the road stories because the young ones learn from them. That's the only reason.

plain.li: The young ones stopped asking about the road a while ago, and I've stopped bringing it up. It's just a thing that happened now.

warm.li: Someone else told my road story at supper tonight, and told it better than I do.

blunt.li: Done with road stories. Everyone's heard them.

cheerful.li: The road stories are retired! I've got new ones now, from right here.

gloomy.li: The road is a long way behind us. I don't talk about it now.

cold.li: The road stories no longer serve a purpose. I've stopped telling them.

plain.li: I've started cutting a small mark into everything I make, low down where nobody looks. My teacher had one too.
Every piece I finish gets my mark now. It means I'm not ashamed of it.

cold.li: I mark my work now. If something fails, they'll know whom to blame. If it lasts, the same.

cheerful.li: I have a maker's mark! It's a little bird. Look under any chair I've made.

warm.li: I mark everything I make now, so whoever uses it knows somebody cared.

blunt.li: My mark's on it. It's mine. It's good.

gloomy.li: I mark my work. When I'm gone, the pieces will still say I was here.

plain.li: I forgot to mark the last few pieces. I don't think I need to any more. People know whose they are.

warm.li: I made a stool for a friend today and didn't mark it. They know who made it.

blunt.li: Stopped marking things. Waste of time.

cheerful.li: No more maker's mark! Now everything I make is a mystery.

gloomy.li: I stopped marking my work. It's not as if anyone checks.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: sets a place for the lost

plain.li: I set an extra bowl at supper now and then, for the one we lost. Last night someone put bread beside it.
On some evenings I lay an extra place at the end of the table, with a cup and a spoon, the way they liked it.

warm.li: There's a place at the table for the one we lost, now and then. The others pass the dishes around it as if someone's sitting there.

gloomy.li: I keep setting a place for the dead. I know how it looks. I'm doing it anyway.

blunt.li: There's a place set for them. Leave it.

cheerful.li: I set a place for them sometimes, and I tell them what's for supper! It's silly, and I like it.

plain.li: I didn't set the extra place last night, and it felt all right. I think they'd have told me to stop fussing a long time ago.

warm.li: I didn't set the extra place tonight. I told them goodbye properly instead.

blunt.li: No extra bowl tonight. It's time.

cheerful.li: I stopped setting their place, but I still save them a joke at supper.

gloomy.li: The extra place is gone from the table. I think about them anyway.

ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.label: the Wanderer
ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.earned: "Ask the Wanderer," people say now, whenever the talk turns to the road. {PAWN_nameDef} came home from it with a new name.

ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.label: Steadyhand
ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.earned: Since the piece {PAWN_possessive} own teacher couldn't fault, {PAWN_nameDef} has been Steadyhand to the rest of the colony.

ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.label: the Unafraid
ColonyCouncil.EpithetDef.earned: {PAWN_nameDef} was afraid for a long time, and then wasn't. The others have started calling {PAWN_objective} the Unafraid.
